chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Ahmad from Musa ibn Umar from Muhammad ibn Mansur from him (the Imam) said:
I asked him about the shade (for the person in Ihram). He said, 'He should not seek shade except due to a weakness or illness.'

key_terms.لِلْمُحْرِمِ: For the person in Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on seeking shade for a Muhrim during Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the prohibition of seeking shade (*al-zilal*) for the *muhrim* is not absolute but contingent upon necessity, specifically citing physical weakness (*'illat*) or illness (*marad*). This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of *raf' al-haraj* (removal of hardship), distinguishing between mere comfort and genuine need, thereby allowing the pilgrim to use umbrellas or trees when heat causes distress or health risks.
